title: [CQ-R12] Safe host admission
description:
Objective: Keep target Git writes in protected wrappers and import only validated candidate bytes.

Deliverable: Safe host admission. This is task R12 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): R01, R09, V02.
definitionOfDone: Disable executable hooks/fsmonitor/filters/helpers and sanitize inherited Git config/environment.
Candidate Moe source cannot replace active host controller.
Host never executes repository tests/package scripts/hooks during admission.

taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
Share R09b's hardened Git envelope from scripts/local-runner/source-export.mjs, without changing export's behavior.

- Export gitRunner(git, root, timeoutMs, {prefix = [], env = {}, fail = () => exportError('EXPORT_GIT_FAILED')} = {}).
  - prefix goes after GIT_PREFIX and safe.directory and before args.
  - env merges over the sanitized env (no inherited GIT_*; GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT as today).
  - fail() replaces both EXPORT_GIT_FAILED rejections.
- Export openRepository({repoDir, git, timeoutMs}, {fail, unsupported, runner}). It holds openCommit's first half: realpath, the '/*' refusal, rev-parse --show-toplevel equality, and the no-scope `config --includes --get-regexp` refusal of partialclone, promisor, core.worktree and filter.*. It returns {root, run}. openCommit calls it and then peels as today.
- Export's argv, env, codes and refusals stay byte-identical: local-runner-snapshot.test.mjs must pass unchanged.
- Error handling: every failure still maps to one fixed code through fail/unsupported, and no Git output or path reaches a message.

No new test in this step. The unchanged snapshot suite is its proof; run `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-snapshot.test.mjs` now for a green baseline after the edit.
implementationPlan.note: Exported gitRunner(git, root, timeoutMs, {prefix, env, fail}) and openRepository({repoDir, git, timeoutMs}, {unsupported, ...runnerOptions}) from source-export.mjs. The second argument is {unsupported} plus gitRunner's own options (prefix/env/fail), a flatter form of the plan's {fail, unsupported, runner}. openCommit now calls openRepository and then peels as before. Export argv, env, codes and refusals are unchanged: local-runner-snapshot.test.mjs passed 22/22 unchanged (env -i, node v24.21.0). Diff: +18/-10. Peers' dirty paths noted and left alone.

New scripts/local-runner/admission.mjs, covering the step-2 part: input checks, the frozen-candidate re-validation, openRepository with the admission envelope, the object-format and base-tree peel (openBase), the ls-tree base map and checkEntries. Rows A1 and A2 are appended to local-runner.test.mjs, with a section-start static import as in the X sections. Both pass (env -i, node 24).

Deviations, each recorded:
(1) The plan row "deleting a with file a/b is allowed" cannot occur. validateImport already refuses a delete above or below a file (SNAPSHOT_PATH_COLLISION, which is source-export's documented v1 D/F limit). A2 pins that upstream refusal instead, and checkEntries checks files against the base directly, which is stricter and simpler.
(2) The prefix also carries -c index.sparse=false: a sparse index could hold directory entries in the private index. This is config sanitization under DoD 1, and A6 will pin it.
(3) Sizes and kinds are compared per entry as well as sha256 and path.
(4) An unknown object format gives ADMISSION_GIT_FAILED; a length mismatch gives ADMISSION_BASE_INVALID.
(5) The A1 temp-dir check runs on every platform, using TMPDIR/TEMP/TMP isolation; the logging-wrapper check runs on POSIX.

Added writeTree to admission.mjs. It writes private 0600 blob copies ('wx'), runs ONE `hash-object -w --no-filters --stdin-paths`, and checks the printed ids against Node's own sha1/sha256 blob hash (else ADMISSION_GIT_FAILED). Then it runs read-tree <base> into the private index, `update-index -z --force-remove --stdin` (deletes), `update-index -z --index-info` (files) and `write-tree`; the id must be full hex of the base's length. admitCandidate resolves a frozen {baseTree, tree, digest}.

TDD: A3 and A4 failed RED against the step-2 module (no tree) and pass now.
- A3: the exact leaves and bytes, with CRLF and $Id$ content kept through `.gitattributes` `* text eol=crlf ident` and local core.autocrlf=true. Also: the exec bit gives 100755; the empty candidate equals the base; two concurrent admissions get their own trees; a sha256 repo works.
- A4: the worktree, .git minus objects/ (index, refs, packed-refs, HEAD, logs, config) and for-each-ref are unchanged. So is the real module's sha256. No marker appears from candidate scripts (moe-agent.sh, postinstall.sh), and the tree holds the candidate bytes.
- A4 import check: admission.mjs and its two siblings import only node: built-ins and each other, with no import( or require(.

Deviation: a `.gitattributes` `filter=x` row was not added. Any filter.* config is refused (A2), and an attribute without its config is a no-op, so ident, eol and autocrlf are the live conversions --no-filters must defeat.

Theoretical notes, not bugs:
- Peak memory is about 3x candidate bytes during re-validation.
- Sequential temp writes count against timeoutMs.
- A concurrent `gc --prune=now` could prune the fresh unreferenced objects. The consumer's read-tree or checkout then fails closed.

- Case-variant paths are a v1 residual for Windows/macOS checkouts.
- Linked worktrees and submodule checkouts are accepted, because openRepository's show-toplevel check holds.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Rejected these options:
1) Admission creates a commit or a ref. Target and branch writes belong to the wrappers' landing (commit-tree plus update-ref CAS), so admission yields a tree only. Later activation (out of scope) commits it.
2) Duplicating R09b's Git envelope. It is shared instead, since the QA-hardened config-scope refusal was hard-won (gotcha-local-runner-tests).
3) One hash-object --stdin per file. Up to 10,000 spawns; --stdin-paths over private temp files is one process.
4) git fast-import. More stream code, and it is built around refs and marks.
5) Relying on update-index's D/F handling. --index-info replaces silently, so conflicts are checked explicitly against the base listing.
6) Allowing a bare 'git'. Windows resolves it against the repo cwd (task-d72fe292).
planningNotes.risks:
- Git-version portability (CI runs ubuntu, windows and macos): --show-object-format needs Git >= 2.27; core.hooksPath to an empty private dir is portable, where /dev/null and NUL are not.
- A6's /bin/sh wrapper is POSIX-only; A1-A5 must pass on Windows.
- Base listings of huge repos hit the runner's 64 MiB maxBuffer and fail closed (SNAPSHOT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED).
- Case-variant collisions against the base are a documented residual, not a v1 refusal.
- The source-export refactor must keep the snapshot suite byte-identical.
- Size is close to 400; never cut rows (see step 5).

completionSummary:
CQ-R12 safe host admission: 400 changed lines.

New scripts/local-runner/admission.mjs, exported admitCandidate({repoDir, baseTree, candidate, git, timeoutMs}):
- Input checks:
  - repoDir and git must be absolute, and git's realpath must lie outside the repository, both checked before any spawn.
  - The candidate must be a frozen validateImport manifest. It is re-derived from its own bytes, and its digest and each entry's kind, path, size and sha256 must match.
- Base checks:
  - baseTree must peel to itself as a tree in the repo's sha1 or sha256 format.
  - A delete must name a base blob.
  - A file may only replace a base blob or add a path that is neither a base directory nor beneath a base symlink, gitlink or blob.
- One tree object is written by plumbing only: hash-object -w --no-filters, checked against Node-computed blob ids, then read-tree, update-index and write-tree.
- Git runs in R09b's envelope:
  - no inherited GIT_*, no system or global config, no replace objects, protocol.allow=never, fsmonitor off;
  - plus an empty private core.hooksPath, a private GIT_INDEX_FILE, and splitIndex and sparse index off.
- A filter, partial clone or core.worktree in any config scope is refused.
- No ref, worktree or .git/index byte changes, and no repository code runs. The temp dir is removed on every path.
- Every refusal is one fixed ADMISSION_* or SNAPSHOT_* code.
- executionReady, verified-local and isolation are untouched.

source-export.mjs now exports gitRunner and openRepository, refactored out of openCommit. Export behaviour is unchanged: snapshot suite 22/22.

Tests A1-A6 in local-runner.test.mjs cover:
- input refusals and forged candidates;
- base conflicts, including gitlinks, symlinks, sha256 and a worktree-scope filter;
- exact bytes under autocrlf, eol and ident;
- concurrency;
- controller-copy candidates;
- hostile hooks, fsmonitor, package scripts, GIT_* and HOME;
- the exact argv and env envelope.
